title: Pentecost
hook: pray for the gifts every year
tomorrow: does God take the summer off when you do?

segments.voice: Yesterday, fifty days of joy, ten more than the fast. Day fifty is where we land today.

Some people want a sign they can feel: goosebumps at the bridge of a song, a voice, a certainty you can't argue with. Acts gives Pentecost signs like that. A sound from heaven like a mighty wind, tongues like fire resting on each of them, and the disciples speaking so that visitors from many nations hear them in their own languages. A Catholic is confirmed once. So why does the Church pray every Pentecost, come, Holy Spirit, as if for the first time?
screen: `A SIGN YOU CAN FEEL.` → `WIND, FIRE, LANGUAGES.` → `CONFIRMED ONCE. WHY ASK AGAIN?`

segments.voice: Two real answers live inside the Church. One view looks first to the quiet gifts. Isaiah names them resting on the coming king, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "the spirit of wisdom, and of understanding, the spirit of counsel, and of fortitude, the spirit of knowledge, and of godliness," and then, "he shall be filled with the spirit of the fear of the Lord." Seven. The catechism calls these gifts lasting dispositions that make a person ready to follow the Spirit's lead. Its best case: the Spirit can work unseen, and chasing a feeling can make you miss what is quietly growing. You grow into the gifts like a muscle you didn't know you had. The other view, alive in the Catholic charismatic renewal, also prays openly for the gifts Paul lists: healing, prophecy, tongues, expected now, not only then. Its best case: Acts isn't just history. The same Spirit comes again, and asking boldly is how the first disciples prayed. Paul holds both in one sentence: "Now there are diversities of graces, but the same Spirit." Here's one to tell a friend tonight: confirmation is never repeated, yet every Pentecost Mass asks again, come, Holy Spirit. Once given, and asked for every year.
screen: `ISAIAH: SEVEN QUIET GIFTS.` · `BEST CASE: THE SPIRIT WORKS UNSEEN.` · `BEST CASE: ASK BOLDLY, LIKE ACTS.` · `DIVERSITIES OF GRACES, SAME SPIRIT.` · then, large: `COME AGAIN.`

segments.voice: Sit with your hands open on your knees, palms up. Choose one gift from Isaiah's list you'd want this year: wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, godliness or fear of the Lord. Hold that one word in your open hands for the sit. If you pray, you can ask for it in your own plain words.
Pentecost. The fiftieth day, when the Spirit came, and the feast that asks for the Spirit again each year.
Your line: come again. One Spirit, many gifts, asked for again every single year. Until tomorrow.
